title: Four Hom comparisons imply Isom comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme, B any commutative ring, and A,D any objects of the derived category of etale B-module sheaves. Suppose each of the four canonical Hom-sheaf comparison maps of [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-sheaf-comparison] for (A,D), (D,A), (A,A), (D,D) is an isomorphism. Then the canonical Isom-sheaf comparison map for (A,D) is an isomorphism. The sheaves are the sheafifications of actual local derived maps and isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-presheaves]. No boundedness, finiteness or weak contractibility is assumed.

proof.text: For any site and two derived objects A,D, form the presheaf of pairs in Hom(A,D) times Hom(D,A). The two arrows to Hom(A,A) times Hom(D,D) are (f,g) -> (fg,gf) and the identity pair. Isom(A,D) is their equalizer. The Lean construction rawPair_limit explicitly supplies its universal lift and proves uniqueness by the forward map. Restriction preserves the compositions and identities.

source.place: Elementary inverse-pair equalizer, implemented on actual local derived maps

proof.text: Sheafification and geometric inverse image preserve the equalizer and the two binary products. The four canonical Hom comparison maps yield the maps between these products. Their squares commute with the relation and identity arrows: check on presheaf classes via the two adjunctions; product_generator proves that a pulled-back pair is precisely the class of the pair of pulled-back maps. Pullback preserves composition and identity.

The canonical Isom comparison commutes with both projections: the first is the forward-map comparison; the second is the inverse-map comparison. The product maps are isomorphisms because all four Hom maps are. Between the two limit forks the induced equalizer map is an isomorphism: use the inverse product map to lift the target equalizer into the source equalizer, then uniqueness proves both inverse equations. The private fork_comparison_isIso implements this argument.
